newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil resists moving higher with crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil resists moving higher with crude.

text.p: NWE cracked fuel oil was broadly steady on Tuesday despite late Monday's cold-weather gains on crude futures.
Dealers said there was uncertainty about the durability of Monday's rises and IPE Brent on Tuesday was some 20 cents off.
High sulphur barges traded around $122 fob ARA, up about $1 from Monday. Demand was seen good, at up to 30,000 tonnes.
"That's the second day of strong buying, but some people feel the market has been inflated," said one barge trader.
"Compared with other ports ARA does look expensive, but against crude it looks good," he added.
Strong demand spread over several days will limit heavy barge gains, dealers said.
The high and low sulphur cracked cargo market remained quiet, although there was unconfirmed talk of a one percent January paper deal done around $130 fob NWE.
The low sulphur market continues to look long with several cargoes available on end Dec and early Jan dates. A handysize cargo loading Jan 3-5 was offered at $127 fob NWE.
